jobs.description:
Description

Job Summary:
While maintaining good public relations and implementing the goals and vision of the regional center, this position is responsible for providing and coordinating services to consumers in accordance with the provisions of the Lanterman Developmental Disabilities Services Act, and policies established by the San Andreas Regional Center Board of Directors.

Essential Job Functions

Gathers data and produces initial and/or ongoing assessments
Presents assessment data to Interdisciplinary Team (IDT) for eligibility determination
Coordinates the Person Centered Planning process with consumers and their families
Counsels consumers concerning identification and achievement of personal goals
Advocates with consumers/families to assure provision of needed services
Initiates and follows up on referrals to existing community resources
Identifies areas of unmet needs
Performs tasks which relate to fiscal and accountability requirements
Provides assistance to existing and in the development of new community services
Develops and facilitates support groups for consumers and/or their families
Completes all required caseload documentation
Develops expertise in accessing generic resources
Assures that all consumers and families are informed verbally and in writing of their right to appeal every time a decision is made to change, alter, or deny a service
Knows Title 17 and Title 22 licensing and DDS requirements
Knows all resources that serve our consumers who reside in various districts
Intervenes effectively in crisis situations in order to eventually effect stability
Monitors residential facilities in compliance with Title 17 regulations
Monitors day programs to assure quality programming

Requirements

Education/Experience:
A Bachelor’s Degree in social work, rehabilitation counseling or a related field from an accredited college or a Bachelor's Degree in Social Work plus four years of experience. The specific field of study for the Bachelor's Degree and the post Bachelor's years of experience may be waived only by the Executive Director if needed by the agency to meet a special need, e.g. services to specific cultural or monolingual groups.

Special Skills and Knowledge:
Knowledge of principles, objectives and techniques of social work; individual and group behavior, human growth, development of family relationships; medical-psycho-socio-economic factors affecting individuals and families; techniques of intervention, referral and follow-up to community resources and facilities and various community organizations, and how to intervene constructively on the client's behalf. Ability to relate in a constructive and enabling manner to a wide variety of individuals and organizations; ability to relate in a positive manner with supervisor, co-workers, and others in the agency and community; establish and maintain rapport with clients and their families; prepare and present oral and written reports; maintain case records in a clear, concise, appropriate and timely manner.

Other:
Use of an automobile, possession of a valid driver's license and automobile liability insurance for the minimum amount prescribed by law, OR ability to provide for independent transportation.

Job Description

MH: Case Management and Social- ( Unscheduled, Varied Shift) -

Job Summary:
The Case Manager serves as a key member of the patient care delivery team and works efficiently in a fast-paced environment and utilizes clinical expertise, discretion and independent judgment in performing the nursing process (assessment, care planning, intervention, evaluation) within a patient-centered care professional practice model (Duffy's Quality-Caring Model) as it relates to case management functions. Maintains a solid working knowledge of specialized case and utilization management methodologies and practices and applies concepts to everyday practice. Ensures medical appropriateness criteria (medical necessity) are met for level of care provided and is documented from admission through discharge. Practices in a collaborative healthcare environment to oversee implementation of a well-thought-out interdisciplinary plan of care with an individualized discharge plan that is comprehensive and best meets the continuing healthcare needs of the patient. Reevaluates plan of care and ensures continued appropriateness based on the patients changing needs and condition. Represents nursing as an empowered profession and readily embraces new knowledge, innovations and improvements. Exhibits positivity and serves as an instrumental change agent and expertly minimizes resistance to change in the workforce, clinical practice and operational setting. Engages in opportunities to directly or indirectly influence decision-making for clinical practice by supporting and participating in committees, task forces and staff meetings. Performs other duties as needed.

Education and Experience:
Bachelor of Science degree in nursing (BSN) required. Minimum two years of hospital nursing experience required. Minimum two years of case management, utilization review, or discharge planning experience in acute care environment preferred.

Knowledge and Skills:
Basic knowledge of case and utilization management practice and methodologies and state and federal healthcare regulations and accreditation required. Able to: speak, read and write legibly in English (and Spanish preferred) with professional quality; use computer, printer and software programs necessary to the position, e.g., Microsoft Office Suite, Outlook, electronic medical record, electronic event reporting program. Relate and communicate positively, effectively and exhibit professional behavior at all times; work calmly and respond courteously when under pressure; be assertive and consistent in following policies; teach, and collaborate; accept direction; think critically; work independently with minimal supervision; perform basic math and statistical functions; manage multiple assignments effectively; organize and prioritize workload; problem solve; recall information with accuracy; pay close attention to detail; hear sufficiently for general conversation in person and on the telephone; identify and distinguish various sounds associated with the work place; see adequately to read computer screens, medical records, and written documents necessary to position.

Licensures and Certifications:
Active and unrestricted California Registered Nurse (RN) license required. Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification issued by the American Heart Association required. Nationally recognized certification in Utilization Management or Case Management preferred.

Job Description

Turner & Townsend is seeking an Associate Program Manager
to support pre-lease technical due diligence for a confidential hyperscale data center client. You will work under a Program Manager to keep a portfolio of live deals organized, on track, and moving, while building toward ownership of your own deals.

This is an execution and organization role that builds into program management. You will own the tracking, follow-up, and day-to-day structure across every deal you support, sit in on every deal call as the account's backstop, and progressively take on direct ownership of workstreams and sites as you demonstrate the judgment to run them. Deals move on short exclusivity windows and incomplete information. We are looking for people who bring order to that rather than waiting for it to settle.

Prior program or project coordination experience is expected. Data center, real estate, or construction exposure is a plus but not required. This is not an executive assistant role and not a purely administrative function. It is the operational backbone of the diligence process, and a defined path into full program management.

This role reports to a Program Manager and is based in San Francisco, with other locations and remote considered for the right candidate.

Responsibilities

Tracking and follow-up:
Own the action item log across every meeting on your accounts. Assign owners, chase status, and close items out, escalating anything that stalls.
Risk log management:
Keep the risk register current for every site in your portfolio. Log new findings, confirm each has an owner and a next step, and follow up until closed.
Meeting management:
Build and distribute the agenda ahead of every standing call, keep it on track, and issue a recap and minutes the same day.
Deliverable tracking:
Track what is due from consultants and developers across every workstream, and chase it before it is late, not after.
Deal awareness and backstop:
Participate in every deal call across your portfolio. Serve as the backstop for each deal, whether you own it or not: know what is happening, what the open issues and risks are, and what needs to happen next. Backstop means knowing it and flagging it, not making the final call on it.
Communication and systems:
Keep the shared trackers and communication channels clean, concise, and accurate so the Program Manager, the client, and other account partners can find what they need without asking you first.
Client and reporting support:
Draft the first pass of client reports and status updates for the Program Manager to edit, so they are reacting to a draft, not starting from a blank page.
Process and tools:
Build and maintain the checklists and templates the account runs on, and improve them yourself when you find a gap.
Deal ownership:
As you ramp, take direct ownership of full workstreams or lower-complexity sites end to end, bringing judgment calls to the Program Manager until you have earned the room to make more of them yourself.
Escalation:
Raise anything that looks wrong the same day it surfaces. Do not sit on an open question hoping it resolves itself.

SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.

Qualifications

Minimum 3 to 5 years of relevant experience. A degree is not required.
Prefer candidates that are located in/near San Francisco, CA that can come to the office 2 to 3 days a week but will consider remote for the right candidates.

Program or project coordination experience preferred. Data center, real estate, or construction backgrounds are a plus.
Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, low-information environment, with the organizational instinct to bring structure to it.

Raise anything that looks wrong the same day it surfaces. Do not sit on an open question hoping it resolves itself.

Who We Are

Oregon Judicial Department (OJD) serves the public, and the people we serve may be facing challenging life circumstances, high levels of stress, or confusion about their next steps. The work you will do in this role affects members of our community who come to the court to have their cases resolved. We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive team and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. Salary offers are made with consideration of the candidate’s education and experience.

Position Highlights

The 10th Judicial District, which includes the Union County Circuit Court in La Grande, Oregon, and the Wallowa County Circuit Court in Enterprise, Oregon, is hiring a Treatment Court Program Manager
(Program Manager). This position will oversee treatment court programs in two locations with their primary office located in the La Grande court offices. This position will be expected to travel frequently to the Enterprise court to provide program support at that location.

In this role, you will meet with treatment court applicants, provide information about the program, perform intake services, and use screening tools to determine eligibility for the program. You will oversee the delivery of program services including referrals, orientation, case planning, and case tracking. You will develop, implement, and monitor program policies, procedures, goals, and standards. You will maintain accurate records of participant files, testing records, and program data and will produce a variety of reports. You will attend court sessions and document appearances and actions taken at each hearing. You will ensure that graduation events are properly planned and resourced to recognize participants’ achievements. You will also identify barriers to program participation and recommend and implement strategies to improve participant access and program outcomes.

Collaboration is a key aspect of this position. You will foster strong working relationships with program participants, court staff, other OJD staff, service providers, behavioral health partners, community partners, district attorneys, defense attorneys, law enforcement and corrections staff, the federal government, and other agencies. You will plan and support program‑related meetings and events, including steering committee meetings, participant graduations, and alumni group activities. You will make presentations about the program to local government and public sector committees. You will also participate in local, regional, state, and national training and education programs to share information about our treatment court program operations.

You will spend part of your time working on special projects, tracking and reporting on program finances, coordinating grant-related activities, and ensuring the program complies with grant requirements.

About This Position

Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) served approximately 52 million passengers in 2025, making it one of the busiest airports in the nation and a major commercial aviation hub for the country's fifth largest city. PHX is the largest of three airports in the Phoenix Airport System along with Deer Valley and Goodyear operated by the City of Phoenix Aviation Department (AVN). Collectively, these airports generate an estimated $38 billion annual economic impact.

The Airside Operations Section ensures PHX's airfield operates safely, efficiently, and in full compliance with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) regulations, including FAR Part 139. Airside Operations oversees daily aircraft movement areas, inspections, safety programs, operational coordination, NOTAM issuance, airfield construction impacts, and regulatory documentation critical to maintaining PHX's Part 139 certification and 24/7 operational readiness.

The Aviation Department is seeking an Airside Operations Program Manager to provide program level leadership across airfield regulatory programs, oversee operational coordination, and manage compliance initiatives that directly support airfield safety and efficiency. This role serves as a key leader in the Airside Operations Section, responsible for aligning airfield programs with departmental goals, supervising multiple operational units, and advancing strategic initiatives that sustain PHX's reputation as a world class airport.

Airside Operations employs field staff, supervisors, and program leaders who support PHX's constant airfield activity. The Airside Operations Program Manager will be instrumental in regulatory compliance, operational excellence, employee development, and cross divisional coordination that strengthens PHX's airfield performance.

Key Duties Include

Program & Strategic Leadership

Provide program-level direction for FAA Part 139 compliance, ensuring policies, inspections, documentation, and safety evaluations meet regulatory requirements.
Lead development of airfield programs aligned with AVN¿s strategic goals, including inspection tracking, safety initiatives, and operational performance measures.
Coordinate program updates, compliance documentation, and strategic recommendations for Section and Division leadership.

Airside Operations & Daily Coordination

Direct and support daily airfield operations to maintain safe and efficient aircraft movement consistent with FAA and airport standards.
Provide expert guidance on complex operational challenges impacting safety, customer service, and regulatory compliance.
Oversee special events, VIP aircraft movements, and irregular operations requiring cross-agency coordination.

Regulatory Compliance & Safety Programs

Manage daily implementation of FAA Part 139 requirements, including inspections, safety risk management, and corrective actions.
Participate in FAA Safety Risk Management (SRM) panels to support hazard identification and mitigation strategies.
Oversee Construction Safety and Phasing Plans (CSPPs) for all airfield construction projects.
Support daily management of the Safety Management System (SMS).

Contractor, Construction, and Project Coordination

Coordinate operational impacts of airfield construction with Engineering, Facilities, contractors, and FAA representatives.
Review and provide guidance on construction phasing, closures, and NOTAM issuance.
Support integration of airfield operational needs into project planning.

Team Development & Collaboration

Supervise Airside Operations Supervisor II positions and provide indirect oversight for Airside Operations Assistants.
Lead recruitment, performance management, and workforce development initiatives.
Coordinate cross-divisional collaboration supporting operational readiness.

Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement

Prepare and present airfield program updates, compliance reports, and operational analyses.
Maintain communication with airlines, tenants, FAA representatives, and contractors.

IDEAL CANDIDATE

Knowledge of the aviation industry.
Familiar with technical writing.
Proficient communicator and capable of managing multiple projects successfully.
Proficient decision-making skills and effective at problem-solving and compliance resolution.
Ability to communication orally and in the English language with customers, clients, and the public in face-to-face, one-on-one, and in group settings.
Strong knowledge of FAA regulations, Safety Management System (SMS) principles, airport construction impacts, and NOTAM processes.
Strong analytical, reporting, and policy development skills with the ability to present clear and concise information to leadership and stakeholder groups.
Demonstrated three (3) years of experience managing FAA Part 139 compliance programs, airfield inspections, and safety risk mitigation activities.
